defs.d: A police officer.
To make somebody busy or active; to occupy.
defs.ex: On my vacation I'll busy myself with gardening.

defs.d: To rush somebody.
Crowded with business or activities; having a great deal going on.
defs.ex: We crossed a busy street.

defs.d: Engaged in activity or by someone else.
defs.ex: He is busy with piano practice.

defs.d: A short written or spoken expression.
(grammar) A word or group of words that functions as a single unit in the syntax of a sentence, usually consisting of a head, or central word, and elaborating words.
To express (an action, thought or idea) by means of particular words.
defs.ex: I wasn't sure how to phrase my condolences without sounding patronising.

defs.d: To perform a passage with the correct phrasing.
A fact or statement used to support a proposition; a reason.
A verbal dispute; a quarrel.
(NNES) To put forward as an argument; to argue.
A rite or ceremony.
Fame, renown; the state of being famous or talked-about.
The break in the working week, usually two days including the traditional holy or sabbath day. Thus in western countries, Saturday and Sunday.
To spend the weekend.
defs.ex: We'll weekend at the beach.

defs.d: Of, relating to or for the weekend.
defs.ex: I'm wearing my weekend shoes.

defs.d: Occurring at the weekend.
defs.ex: a weekend break

defs.d: The act or process of explaining.
defs.ex: The explanation was long and drawn-out.

defs.d: Something that explains, makes understandable.
defs.ex: An explanation for the UFO sightings was easily found.

defs.d: The lumbar region; loin.
(of a person or animal) The loins; flank; buttocks.
To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to bother with unpleasant deeds.
defs.ex: Marc loved his sister, but when she annoyed him he wanted to switch her off.

defs.d: To do something to upset or anger someone; to be troublesome.
That which annoys; an annoyance.
Causing irritation or annoyance; troublesome; vexatious.
defs.ex: Vandals are really annoying.

defs.d: A strong feeling of anxiety.
defs.ex: I'm afflicted by worry throughout the night.

defs.d: An instance or cause of such a feeling.
defs.ex: My main worry is that I'll miss the train.

defs.d: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.
defs.ex: Stop worrying about your test, it’ll be fine.

defs.d: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress.
defs.ex: Your tone of voice worries me.

defs.d: To inquire into or study in order to ascertain facts or information.
defs.ex: to investigate the causes of natural phenomena

defs.d: To examine, look into, or scrutinize in order to discover something hidden or secret.
defs.ex: to investigate an unsolved murder

defs.d: Popularly or widely.
defs.ex: It is generally known that the Earth is round.

defs.d: As a rule; usually.
defs.ex: I generally have a walk in the afternoon.

defs.d: An unexpected occurrence; a surprise.
Happening quickly and with little or no warning.
defs.ex: The sudden drop in temperature left everyone cold and confused.

defs.d: Hastily prepared or employed; quick; rapid.
Suddenly.

Evidence of a long-term debt, by which the bond issuer (the borrower) is obliged to pay interest when due, and repay the principal at maturity, as specified on the face of the bond certificate. The rights of the holder are specified in the bond indenture, which contains the legal terms and conditions under which the bond was issued. Bonds are available in two forms: registered bonds, and bearer bonds.
A documentary obligation to pay a sum or to perform a contract; a debenture.
defs.ex: Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.

defs.d: To connect, secure or tie with a bond; to bind.
defs.ex: The gargantuan ape was bonded in iron chains and carted onto the stage.

defs.d: To cause to adhere (one material with another).
defs.ex: The children bonded their snapshots to the scrapbook pages with mucilage.

defs.d: An advisement providing more up-to-date information than currently known.
defs.ex: He gave me an update on the situation in New York.

defs.d: A change in information, a modification of existing or known data.
defs.ex: I just made an update to the Wikipedia article on guerillas.

defs.d: To bring (a thing) up to date.
defs.ex: I need to update my records to take account of the most recent transaction.

defs.d: To bring (a person) up to date: to inform (a person) about recent developments.
defs.ex: Update me on what happened while I was away.

defs.d: At depth, in a deep way.
To a deep extent.
Destiny, especially favorable.
defs.ex: She read my fortune. Apparently I will have a good love life this week, but I will have a bad week for money.

defs.d: A prediction or set of predictions about a person's future provided by a fortune teller.
To happen, take place.
To provide with a fortune.
The act of judging.
The power or faculty of performing such operations; especially, when unqualified, the faculty of judging or deciding rightly, justly, or wisely
defs.ex: a man of judgment

defs.d: To keep in possession or use.
To keep in one's pay or service.
